messages:
Maya: Heads up — prod alert: rpc_tool_v2 schema rejections spiked to 6.2% over the last hour, mostly from region eu-west-1. sample log: `invoke_id=abc123 schema_error=missing_field('metadata.user_id')`
Sophie: saw the alert, pages went out. latency looks normal, just validation rejects. any recent rollout?
Jamal: we rolled strict-schema=true for the rpc_tool_v2 canary yesterday at 10:12. only 5% of traffic was on the canary but looks like it propagated to more via routing fallback? investigating.
Elena: product impact? which customers see failures vs graceful fallback?
Maya: console shows a bunch of 4xx rejects but the dashboard groups them as "validation" — doesn't surface example payloads or which route/policy triggered fallback. ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-7321 (auto)
Ravi: we intended strict=canary to only apply to pinned tenants, not global. config snippet we pushed: ```yaml
canary:
  strict_schema: true
  percent: 5
  route: weighted-routing
```
Maya: exact — but weighted-routing fallback policy currently lets requests move to strict variant if adapter returns 503 from primary. that could explain spread.
Jamal: yep, routing policy bug: fallback decision used model-level flags instead of route-level binding. I'll open a patch to check route.bindings when deciding variant fallback.
Sophie: for short-term mitigation can we toggle strict-schema=false on rpc_tool_v2 or set canary.percent=0? which has faster exp?
Ravi: setting canary.percent=0 is config-only and can deploy via console in ~2m (hot config). toggling strict_schema=false requires a code path change and a restart of the canary process (~10-15m).
Elena: do hot rollback now. also we need better telemetry slots: example rejected payload + top offending customer id (hashed) + route id in the dashboard. right now we just have counts which is worthless for triage.
Maya: agreed. proposed console changes (short term): 1) expose a sampling of up to 5 rejected payloads per hour (redacted), 2) add "route_id" and "policy_decision" as first-class columns on the validation errors table, 3) show a tiny histogram of rejects by tenant.
Ravi: fine, but privacy: payloads must be redacted server-side (PII scrub). we can reuse existing redaction pipeline from request-logs.
Jamal: for longer-term, suggest we change routing fallback semantics: never consider variant if it's part of a canary unless explicitly bound to route with allow-fallback=true. that prevents canary bleed.
Sophie: also add an alert rule that looks for simultaneous increase in validation rejects and canary traffic percent > X. current alert only looks at rejects absolute which makes it noisy.
Maya: action items: (1) Ravi to hot-set canary.percent=0 for rpc_tool_v2 now (2) Jamal to open PR for routing bug + unit test (3) Devex to add rejected-payload sampling to console (Ravi) (4) Sophie to add correlated alert rule and write short runbook entry — owners?
Ravi: I'll flip canary.percent=0 in 30s and push a dashboard widget for rejected payload samples by EOD.
Jamal: PR opened: https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/pull/452 — fixes route binding in fallback decision. adding tests.
Elena: thanks team. please add a short note to rollout playbook: "when enabling strict schema canaries, ensure route-level bindings and telemetry sampling enabled"
Maya: noted. I'll update the playbook and follow up with a short console mock for the rejected-sample UI tomorrow. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident INC-2025-7321 status -> mitigated (hot rollback applied)
Sophie: monitoring looks stable after canary.percent=0, rejects back to baseline ~0.4%. closing loop once PR merged and playbook updated.
Maya: perfect — marking follow-ups in Asana and closing the incident after playbook + PR verification.
